([[Brentwood, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 5 | draft_team = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | career_start = 2019 | years1 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team2 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * 2× [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] ({{nasg|2022}}, {{nasg|2025}}) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) * 3× [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2016–2018) }} '''Darius Kinnard Garland''' (born January 26, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]]. Born in Gary, Indiana, Garland is the son of former professional basketball player [[Winston Garland]]. Garland attended [[Brentwood Academy]] in high school, joining the varsity basketball team in eighth grade and leaving as a four-time state champion and three-time [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] winner. He was a five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]], ranked among the best [[point guard]]s in the 2018 class, and a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. He is a two-time NBA All-Star. Garland committed to Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball. After five games, his college career was cut short by a [[Tear of meniscus|meniscus injury]], which prompted him to leave the team to prepare for the NBA draft. After criticism in his first season due to perceived disappointing play, Garland was named to his first [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] Game in 2022, and finished third in voting for the NBA's [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] award the same year. He was named an All-Star again in 2025. ==Early life== Garland was born in [[Gary, Indiana]], to Felicia Garland and former NBA player [[Winston Garland]]. He grew up playing [[baseball]] and started basketball at age five but soon narrowed down his focus to only the latter sport.{{cite web |title=Darius Garland |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/g/garland-darius-1.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611100125/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/g/garland-darius-1.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 11, 2016 |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=January 2, 2019 |date=March 13, 2018}} Garland continued with basketball in elementary school and scored his first basket in second grade.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Darius Garland is Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2016/04/17/darius-garland-boys-basketball-player-year/82668248/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=January 3, 2019 |date=April 17, 2016}} In third grade, he attended basketball camps in [[Valparaiso, Indiana]] led by [[Bryce Drew]], who would become his college coach at [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]].{{cite web |last1=Rexrode |first1=Joe |title=Darius Garland, Rick Byrd and an epic day for Nashville basketball |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2017/11/14/darius-garland-rick-byrd-and-epic-day-nashville-basketball/861176001/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=January 25, 2019 |date=November 14, 2017}} Garland played on a travel team against older opponents and joined an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) squad based in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] when he was in fourth grade, because none of the local teams met his standards.{{cite web |last1=Hutton |first1=Mike |title=Gary's Darius Garland turns into Brentwood's latest basketball savant |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/columnists/ct-ptb-mike-hutton-column-st-0129-20170128-column.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=January 28, 2017}} After he completed sixth grade, his family moved to Tennessee so that he could attend [[Brentwood Academy]] in [[Brentwood, Tennessee]] with his AAU teammates Gavin Schoenwald and [[Camron Johnson]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Darius Garland of Brentwood Academy commits to Vanderbilt basketball |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/11/13/report-brentwood-academys-darius-garland-commits-vanderbilt/815173001/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=January 25, 2019 |date=November 13, 2017}} Garland's father described, "We had always talked about relocating. My mother had lived in Tennessee and she liked it. I just talked to the family and everybody was on board. It was a big leap of faith." ==High school career== Garland joined the starting lineup for the Brentwood Academy [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball team while in eighth grade.{{cite web |last1=Pulliam |first1=Charles |title=Brentwood Academy standout Garland chooses Vanderbilt |url=http://www.williamsonherald.com/sports/article_0f76026a-c8c0-11e7-ad01-0b42709ac4e7.html |website=Williamson Herald |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=November 13, 2017}} In his freshman season, he averaged 17 [[point (basketball)|points]], 1.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2.7 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] per game, leading his team to a [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association]] (TSSAA) Division II-AA state championship.{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=BA's Darius Garland named to USA Junior National Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/bas-darius-garland-named-to-usa-junior-national-team |newspaper=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=April 23, 2015 |archive-date=April 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406225949/https://usatodayhss.com/2015/bas-darius-garland-named-to-usa-junior-national-team |url-status=dead }} Garland was one of three finalists for [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] among Division II-AA players.{{cite web |title=TSSAA's Division II Mr. and Miss Basketball are announced |url=https://www.columbiadailyherald.com/sports/preps/tssaa-s-division-ii-mr-and-miss-basketball-are-announced |website=[[Daily Herald (Columbia, Tennessee)|Daily Herald]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=March 1, 2015 |archive-date=January 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129065516/https://www.columbiadailyherald.com/sports/preps/tssaa-s-division-ii-mr-and-miss-basketball-are-announced |url-status=dead }} On December 23, 2015, as a sophomore, he claimed [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at the King of the Bluegrass Holiday Classic, after scoring 23 points versus [[Fairdale High School]] in the title game.{{cite news |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=King of the Bluegrass: Brentwood Academy beats Trinity for title |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/king-of-the-bluegrass-brentwood-academy-beats-trinity-for-title |newspaper=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=December 23, 2015}} Garland averaged 18.6 points and 4.3 assists per game and earned TSSAA Division II-AA Mr. Basketball accolades. High school sports website [[MaxPreps]] also included him in its Sophomore All-American Team honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=2015-16 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/FNPGNr8ro0KhVZ-LBt_WIQ/2015-16-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=April 20, 2016}} From his sophomore to junior year, he grew 2½ inches, and by his fourth season with Brentwood Academy, he was ranked the best [[point guard]] in the 2018 class by [[college recruiting|recruiting]] service [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Nation's top junior point guard Darius Garland still yet to reach his peak |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/nations-top-junior-point-guard-darius-garland-still-yet-to-reach-his-peak |newspaper=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=January 27, 2019 |date=January 5, 2017}} In March 2017, Garland garnered [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Trophy]] High School All-America honorable mention recognition.{{cite news |title=Naismith Trophy High School Boys All-America team announced |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/naismith-trophy-high-school-boys-all-america-team-announced |newspaper=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=March 8, 2017}} He averaged 23.4 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.1 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and led his team to a 30–2 record and state championship. Garland additionally earned MaxPreps Junior All-American first team distinction.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/otwRLm_KeEGHwC460kRRPg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=April 11, 2017}} On November 13, 2017, he committed to play college basketball for Vanderbilt, drawn there by its proximity to his home and head coach Bryce Drew. Entering his senior season, Garland appeared in the [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA]] preseason team.{{cite news |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=2017-18 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Preseason Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/2017-18-american-family-insurance-all-usa-preseason-boys-basketball-team |newspaper=[[USA Today|USA Today High School Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=November 27, 2017}} He averaged 27.6 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.7 steals and secured a fourth straight state title for Brentwood Academy, tying the TSSAA record.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/vpYHC6-v2kiq_nCltCL9_Q/2017-18-maxpreps-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=April 10, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Darius Garland |url=https://vucommodores.com/404-1.aspx?url=/roster.aspx?rp_id=4300 |publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015114521/https://vucommodores.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4300 |archive-date=October 15, 2018}} Garland joined the MaxPreps High School All-American third team and became the only player other than [[Brandan Wright]] to win Tennessee Mr. Basketball on three occasions. In March 2018, he was named Gatorade Tennessee Player of the Year and a semifinalist for the Naismith Trophy.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Vanderbilt signee Darius Garland named Gatorade Tennessee Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/08/darius-garland-named-gatorade-tennessee-boys-basketball-player-year/407831002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}} On March 28, Garland recorded a game-high 11 assists at the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web |title=Darius Garland has stellar McDonald's Game |url=https://vucommodores.com/news/2018/3/29/Darius_Garland_has_stellar_McDonald_amp_8217_s_Game.aspx?path=mbball |publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=March 29, 2018}} He took part in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] as well. {{College athlete recruit }} ==College career== Garland was the only freshman in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) to make the preseason all-conference team.{{Cite web|url=https://vucommodores.com/news/2018/11/6/mens-basketball-darius-garland-named-as-second-team-preseason-all-sec-selection.aspx|title=Darius Garland named as Second-Team Preseason All-SEC selection - Vanderbilt University|date=November 6, 2018|publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]]|language=en|access-date=November 9, 2018}} On November 6, 2018, in his first college game against [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]], Garland led all scorers with 24 points.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401082918|title=Winthrop vs. Vanderbilt - Box Score - November 6, 2018 - ESPN|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=November 9, 2018}} In a 79–70 win over [[Liberty Flames men's basketball|Liberty]] on November 19, he scored a season-high 33 points, the second-most points by a freshman in school history.{{cite web |last1=Sparks |first1=Adam |title=How Darius Garland's 33 points nearly broke Vanderbilt record in his fourth game |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2018/11/19/vanderbilt-basketball-darius-garland-bryce-drew-liberty/1968914002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=November 19, 2018}} Garland injured his knee during a [[layup]] versus [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]] on November 23 and left the game early.{{cite web |title=Vanderbilt Star Freshman Darius Garland Injured in Loss to Kent State |url=https://www.si.com/2018/11/23/ap-bkc-kent-state-vanderbilt |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |date=November 23, 2018}} Four days later, Vanderbilt head coach [[Bryce Drew]] revealed that Garland would be sidelined for the remainder of the season with a [[tear of meniscus|meniscus injury]].{{Cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25391948/vanderbilt-commodores-pg-darius-garland-miss-rest-season-meniscus-injury-left-knee|title=Vanderbilt's Darius Garland out for remainder of season|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 27, 2018 |access-date=November 27, 2018}} On January 22, 2019, he announced that he would leave Vanderbilt to recover from his injury and prepare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Sparks|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/sounds-cavaliers-draft-darius-garland-231413197.html|title=Sounds like Cavaliers will draft Darius Garland No. 5 if they don't trade pick|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 20, 2019|archive-date=June 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621174304/https://sports.yahoo.com/sounds-cavaliers-draft-darius-garland-231413197.html|url-status=dead}} Garland later became one of 77 total invitees to take part in the [[NBA Draft Combine]].[https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/08/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine] However, he left the event early on May 15, with the notion that he got promised a selection by a team in the NBA draft lottery.[https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/nba-draft-2019-darius-garland-fuels-lottery-speculation-by-leaving-combine/wtjvwq3vvty11stf70mx6aptg NBA Draft 2019: Darius Garland fuels lottery speculation by leaving combine] ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2026)=== ==== Early years (2019–2021) ==== [[File:Darius Garland (48835947106) (cropped).jpg|150px|thumb|right|Garland at the opening of [[Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse]] in 2019]] Garland was selected with the fifth pick by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavs-draft-picks-190620|title=Cavs Select Darius Garland, Dylan Windler in 2019 NBA Draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2019}} On July 3, 2019, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/draft-picks-signings-190703|title=Cavaliers Sign Garland, Windler and Porter Jr.|date=July 3, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 3, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, Garland made his debut in the NBA, starting in an 85–94 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]] with eight points, two rebounds, five assists and a steal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160627|title=Magic, Vucevic beat Cavaliers in season opener|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019}} Garland made history during this game by becoming the first player born in the 2000s to make his NBA debut.{{cite web|url=https://flurrysports.org/darius-garland-makes-history-in-nba-debut/|title= Darius Garland Makes History in NBA Debut|date=October 25, 2019|website=FlurrySports|access-date=January 8, 2021}} On November 22, he scored a season-high 23 points, alongside four assists, in a 101–143 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |title=DONCIC ROLLS WITH NOWITZKI WATCHING, MAVS ROUT CAVS 143-101 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900221 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} During his rookie season, Garland was often ranked amongst the NBA's worst players.{{Cite web |title=Darius Garland was the NBA's worst player. Should he get a pass for horrible rookie season? |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2020/06/darius-garland-was-the-nbas-worst-player-should-he-get-a-pass-for-horrible-rookie-season.html |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Cleveland.com}} He finished his rookie season averaging 12.3 points and 3.9 assists per game. Garland was excluded from both of the season-end [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie]] teams.{{Cite web |title=Report: Darius Garland 'Feels Snubbed and Disrespected' by Exclusion From All-Rookie Teams |url=https://cavaliersnation.com/2020/09/22/darius-garland-snubbed-disrepected-being-excluded-all-rookie-teams/ |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Cavaliers Nation}} On December 23, 2020, Garland made his season debut for the Cavaliers, recording 22 points, six rebounds and six assists in a 121–114 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |title=LAMELO SCORELESS IN DEBUT, CAVS OUTLAST HORNETS IN OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000010 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On April 5, 2021, he scored a then career-high 37 points, along with seven assists in a 125–101 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2021/04/darius-garlands-career-night-helps-end-cleveland-cavaliers-losing-streak-beat-san-antonio-spurs-125-101.html|website=cleveland.com|title=Darius Garland's career night helps Cleveland Cavaliers end losing streak, beat San Antonio Spurs, 125-101 |last=Fedor|first=Chris|date=April 4, 2021|access-date=January 16, 2022}} Despite the Cavaliers missing the playoffs for a third straight season, Garland averaged 17.4 points per game, alongside 6.1 assists and 1.2 steals. ==== First All-Star and playoff appearance (2021–2024) ==== On January 12, 2022, Garland recorded his first career triple-double, putting up 11 points, 10 rebounds, and a then career-high 15 assists, in a 111–91 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://cavsnation.com/cavs-news-donovan-mitchell-hops-darius-garland-all-star-bandwagon/|title=Donovan Mitchell hops on Cavs' Darius Garland All-Star bandwagon|website=ClutchPoints|last=Patt|first=Jason|date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 14, 2022}} On January 15, Garland recorded 27 points and a career-high 18 assists in a 107–102 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2022/01/darius-garland-helps-ignite-cleveland-cavaliers-rally-from-18-point-deficit-in-107-102-win-vs-oklahoma-city-thunder.html|title=Darius Garland ignites Cleveland Cavaliers' rally from 18-point deficit in 107-102 win over Oklahoma City Thunder|website=cleveland.com|last=Bielik|first=Tim|date=January 15, 2022|access-date=January 16, 2022}} On February 3, he was selected to his first [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] Game as a reserve.{{Cite web|title=Darius Garland Selected as All-Star Reserve for 2022 All-Star Game in Cleveland|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/all-star-reserves-220203|access-date=2022-02-09|website=Cleveland Cavaliers|language=en}} On March 8, Garland scored a then career-high 41 points with 13 assists in a 127–124 win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360795 |title=Garland scores career-high 41, leads Cavs past Pacers |agency=Associated Press |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 9, 2022 |accessdate=April 3, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220321072448/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360795 |archive-date=March 21, 2022}} On April 12, Garland scored a team-leading 34 points in a 115–108 [[NBA play-in tournament]] loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401428070 Irving, Durant lead Nets past Cavs in play-in for No. 7 seed] The following game, Garland and the Cavaliers lost to the [[Atlanta Hawks]],[https://www.nba.com/game/atl-vs-cle-0052100201 Young's 38 lift Hawks past Cavs for No. 8 playoff seed] meaning that despite doubling their previous season's win total from 22 to 44 and finishing with the eighth best record in the eastern conference,[https://www.nba.com/resources/static/team/v2/cavaliers/220412-clebkn-notes.pdf CLEVELAND CAVALIERS (44-38)] they would not advance to the postseason. Garland later finished third, behind [[Ja Morant]] and [[Dejounte Murray]], in voting for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] award.{{Cite web |title=Ja Morant Topped Darius Garland And Dejounte Murray To Win The NBA's Most Improved Player Award |url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/ja-morant-nba-most-improved-player-2021-22-award-memphis-grizzlies-voting/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |website=Uproxx}} [[File:Darius Garland (51913955152).jpg|thumb|Garland at the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]]]] On July 9, 2022, Garland signed a five-year, $231M designated rookie extension with the Cavaliers.{{Cite web |title=Darius Garland signs multi-year extension with Cavaliers |url=https://www.nba.com/news/darius-garland-agrees-to-5-year-rookie-maximum-extension-with-cavaliers |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2022-07-02 |title=Cavs All-Star Garland gets max rookie extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34184339/cleveland-cavaliers-darius-garland-agree-five-year-rookie-extension-worth-231m-agent-says |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On November 13, he scored a career-high 51 points, with 27 points scored in the fourth quarter, including a personal record 10-of-15 three-point shots in a 129–124 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He became the fourth Cavaliers player to score 50, joining [[LeBron James]] (nine times), [[Kyrie Irving]] (twice) and [[Walt Wesley]] (once). His ten 3-pointers doubled his previous single-game high and were one short of Irving's team record. He also became the youngest player to score 50+ points and hit 10+ threes in a game before turning 25.{{Cite web |title=Darius Garland Scores A Career-High 51 Points In Loss To Minnesota |url=https://www.si.com/nba/cavaliers/news/darius-garland-scores-a-career-high-51-points-in-loss-to-minnesota |access-date=November 13, 2022 |website=si.com}}{{cite web |title=Garland's career-high 51 not enough, Cavs lose to Wolves |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468348 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=November 14, 2022 |date=November 13, 2022}} On November 18, Garland led the Cavaliers to a double-overtime 132–122 win against the [[Charlotte Hornets]] with a game-leading 41 points.[https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2022/11/cleveland-cavaliers-find-a-way-to-win-2ot-thriller-snap-skid-behind-the-numbers.html Cleveland Cavaliers find a way to win 2OT thriller, snap skid] Garland helped the Cavaliers earn the No. 4 seed in the Eastern Conference, securing home-court advantage in the first round and achieving their first 50-win season since 1993 without [[LeBron James]] on the roster.{{cite web|title=Mitchell scores 43 to lead Cavs to 117-113 win over Magic|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469333|website=ESPN.com|language=en|date=April 4, 2023|access-date=April 9, 2023|archive-date=April 9, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409125638/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469333|url-status=live}} ==== Second All-Star selection and best Eastern Conference record (2024–2026)==== On January 30, 2025, Garland was named as reserve for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his second selection.{{cite web| title= Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves | website=NBA.com | date=January 30, 2025 | url= https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves | access-date=February 2, 2025}} On February 5, 2025, Garland recorded 25 points, five assists and hit a 31-foot 3-pointer at the buzzer to give the Cavaliers a 118–115 win over the [[2024–25 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |title=Garland's deep buzzer-beating 3-pointer gives Cavs 118-115 win over Pistons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705284 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=February 5, 2024 |date=February 5, 2024}} Garland helped lead the Cavaliers to the best record in the Eastern Conference at 64–18, the second-best regular season record in franchise history. In the playoffs, Garland struggled with injuries, and the Cavaliers were upset by the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]] in five games in the Eastern Conference Semifinals for the second year in a row, ending their postseason run earlier than expected. On June 9, Garland underwent surgery on the injured left big toe that had hampered him during Cleveland's playoff exit. Garland is expected to spend 4-to-5 months going through a progression of treatment and rehabilitation before resuming basketball activities by the start of training camp.{{cite web| title= Cavaliers guard Darius Garland undergoes surgery on injured left toe | website=NBA.com | date=June 9, 2025 | url= https://www.nba.com/news/cavs-darius-garland-toe-surgery | access-date=June 9, 2025}} Garland made 26 starts for the Cavaliers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 18.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 6.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Darius Garland 2025-26 Stats per
